answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each agent to a Wesolowski VDF: a challenge-derived value must pass through a prescribed chain of dependent modular squarings before acceptance. Since each step depends on the preceding result, GPUs cannot divide one chain into parallel work; simulating many clones requires many complete chains and multiplies elapsed physical time. Whether deployed near a lagoon, on a knoll, or in a basalt facility, Sybil identities therefore remain costly and time-bounded.
